name: Kayapo
catalog_quote: 5. INTENSIDADE. A Intensidade não é predizível em termos fonológicos. Gramaticalmente, ocorre normalmente na última sílaba do tema da palavra. /pu'nu/ 'mal' /pu'nu-řɛ/ 'mauzinho'

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: confirmed verbatim on the page image of the scan we hold, Stout & Thomson 1974:163 §5, suffix -řɛ as the editor noted. (2) Deciding source is a 1974 SIL phonemic article; it is the classic source but we also HOLD the best modern description (Costa 2015 UnB PhD grammar, pp.45-46: primary stress 'com maior frequência' on the word-final syllable, exceptions = extrametrical suffixes like atenuativo -ɾɛ [puˈnuɾɛ] and echo-vowel forms — the same puˈnu / puˈnu-ɾɛ pair as Stout & Thomson) and I downloaded Salanova & Nikulin 2020:69 ('o acento em Mẽbêngôkre recai na última sílaba, com raríssimas exceções'; unstressed enclitic =re, post-tonic epenthetic vowels, falling diphthongs). Three independent descriptions (1974 Txukahamãe, 2015 Xikrín, 2020 pan-dialectal) agree: regular final stress on the stem/lexical word, weight-blind, with a closed set of unstressed post-stem elements. Our kind 'fi

sources.citation: Stout, Mickey & Ruth Thomson 1974, "Fonêmica Txukuhamẽi (Kayapó)", Série Lingüística 3 (SIL, Brasília), pp. 153-176; stress statement at p. 163 (section 5, INTENSIDADE). Accessed as scanned PDF from Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú: https://etnolinguistica.wdfiles.com/local--files/biblio:stout-19…
sources.quote: "5. INTENSITY [= stress]. Intensity is not predictable in phonological terms. Grammatically, it normally occurs on the last syllable of the stem of the word. /pu'nu/ 'bad'; /pu'nu-re/ 'bad-DIMINUTIVE (a little bad)'."

sources.quote: 'Finalmente, o acento em Mẽbêngôkre recai na última sílaba, com raríssimas exceções.' Exceptions listed: (i) obligatory vowel epenthesis after underlying final /ɾ/ creates a few post-tonic syllables; (ii) words ending in falling diphthongs surface with stress on the penultimate vowel (ngija [ˈŋija], kruwa [ˈkɾuwa]); (iii) unstressed enclitics, notably diminutive =re (vs. tonic augmentative -ti), yield non-final stress in the phonological word. Fn.12: compounds keep secondary stress on each subordinate stem, primary on the last ([ˌɾɔmˈnɔ] 'lanterna').
sources.locator: p.69 (section on phonological shape of native lexicon); also fn.12 p.65 on secondary stress in compounds
